title: Florida's 27th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Florida's 27th Congressional District is a competitive seat covering parts of Miami-Dade County, including Coral Gables, Key Biscayne, and parts of Miami. The district has a history of close races and is currently represented by Republican Maria Elvira Salazar, who is running for re-election. The race is expected to be a key battleground in the 2026 midterms, with national implications for control of the House. The district has a significant Hispanic population and leans Republican but has shown Democratic competitiveness in recent cycles.
polling_note: No public opinion polls found for this race as of early 2026.

candidates.name: Maria Elvira Salazar
candidates.summary: Maria Elvira Salazar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Florida's 27th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She is a former journalist and television anchor, and has focused on issues such as economic growth, immigration reform, and support for Israel. Salazar is seeking re-election in 2026.

career_history.title: Journalist and Television Anchor
career_history.description: Worked as a journalist and anchor for networks including Telemundo and CNN en Español

candidates.name: Lucia Baez-Geller
candidates.summary: Lucia Baez-Geller is a Democratic candidate running for Florida's 27th Congressional District in 2026. She is a former school board member and educator, and has focused on education, healthcare, and environmental issues. Baez-Geller previously ran for this seat in 2022.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race as of June 2026. The forecast relies entirely on district context and candidate backgrounds. Florida's 27th is a competitive Miami-Dade seat described as leaning Republican but with a history of close races and Democratic competitiveness in recent cycles. Incumbent Maria Elvira Salazar (R) benefits from incumbency and two re-election wins (2022, 2024) in a district with a slight Republican lean. Challenger Lucia Baez-Geller (D), a former school board member, ran here in 2022 and lost by ~14 points. The absence of polling, combined with a midterm cycle whose national environment is difficult to assess this far out, results in very high uncertainty. The narrow Republican edge reflects incumbency and district lean, but the margin of uncertainty is large.
